Hit Cryo for 1 damage, then redirect the last hit of his attack to Cryo Bot, which will trigger his attack again, interrupting WtM's Damage to it.  Repeat till it is at 1hp then let WtM destroy it.Works awesomely with +1 to Cryo Bot's damage, since you can hit every non-hero target save 1 6 times for 3 damage (increasing 2 to 3 for all but the redirected shot to Cryo, which you reduce to 1).Best I've pulled off with it was with Legacy giving it +2 and an epic turn by Adept gave Cryo -1 taken, with WtM and TtE getting played.Ennead hit Cryo for 2-1 damage, and Cryo hit them all for 24 damage, leaving an environment target unharmed.  
So, does the stacked damage from WtM still resolve after Cryo-bot dies? As in, when doing this combo, does Visionary take 30+ damage at the end, or does the destruction of Cryo-bot trigger the destruction of WtM before any damage hits Visionary? No.  Once a card leaves play, it stops dealing damage, and WtM leaves play before it gets a chance to hit Visionary.  Visionary would not take damage.

posts.name: nyrens
posts.cooked:
Also, if a villain or environment card makes Chrono Ranger hit himself... well, let's just say it's bad and leave it at that. The special thing about Setback's boost is that only damage to and by villain targets is affected, not all damage. Legacy's Lead From the Front only allows you to redirect damage done by villain targets, but that's fine because that's all you need to protect Setback from. He takes normal damage from non-villain sources, and +1000004 from villains once you get the combo going.

By the by, the other great part of the combo (and this is also true for protecting Chrono Ranger) is that both Lead From the Front and High Risk Behavior are Ongoings, so when a villain or environment destroys hero ongoings, you can almost always choose to blow up High Risk Behavior before Lead From the Front, stopping Setback's human shield from suddenly vanishing mid-villain-turn. Well, unless Legacy is incapacitated... I mean, he is taking double damage from villain AoEs. But, when Legacy's HP starts getting low, you can cancel the combo by dropping Silver Lining, then using Uncharmed Life to redirect damage targetting Legacy to hit Setback instead until it kills him (it won't take much), clearing his Unlucky Pool and thus all his bonus damage taken.

Oh, and on top of the already mentioned combos, throw in Setback's Cause and Effect while he has 24+ tokens (3 rounds worth) and Legacy has Heroic Interception out. 24 tokens with 2x High Risk Behavior out = 40 damage from Cause and Effect, and Heroic Interception protects him from the backlash.

 

Legacy is amazing at protecting fools from hurting themselves. Setback is a fool who constantly hurts himself. Great combo! :D Other people can protect Setback, but Greatest Legacy is special in that he 1) can let Setback use a power out of turn every turn, and 2) has a redirection card that lasts more than one turn (no one else has this (except Setback)). I guess Mainstay's Human Shield works too, but that has a high upkeep. Stealth Bot technically works too, but won't survive Setback being Setback for every long with only 5 HP...

Here's a  new one for me:
Ambuscade opens up with two sonic mines. Visionary starts with Wrest the Mind.

posts.name: phantaskippy
posts.cooked:
Guise + PW Fanatic.

It is so very broken, even more so than Guise + Fixer.  Just amazing. 

1.  Total Beefcake + I can do that too->Resolute = Money for nothing!  Redirect that 3 damage, then put your top card into play, then use a power for Tough Choices.  It's my favorite out of turn play on a big Guise throwdown round, just don't be X-treeeeeeeeme!!! when you do it, but by all means be mighty and fearsome like the fabled Alpaca.

2.  Uh Yeah, I'm that (lady). . . + End of Days = Guise Bot!  Guise's turn needs to be before Fanatic's.  Copy Fanatic, then have Fanatic play End of Days.  Start of Env. turn Guise's text will activate first, since it was in play first, destroy every card you want to destroy, then destroy Fanatic's End of Days, at which point the text of End of days leaves Guise's card and the destruction stops. (he's actually a Hornet)

3.  Uh Yeah, I'm that (lady). . . + Divine Focus = Moar Damages!  Pretty self explanatory there.  Barbarian makes it even better, made Progeny rage quit with this combo.  Also if you have Guise before Fanatic and Total Beefcake in play after Uh, Yeah, then you can opt to take that 4 damage and redirect it.

4.  Uh Yeah, I'm that (lady). . . + Total Beefcake + Sacrosanct Martyr = RPG Trope!  Who doesn't like a power that deals the lowest HP non-hero target 5 radiant damage?  Although I have a feeling Helena isn't going to like the guy in the chainmail bikini passing himself off as her, maybe if he was also a Barbarian she'd be okay with it.

 

I know Guise has lots of combos, but these are just sick.  Resolute may be the best base power to copy in the game, because Guise loves his cards, all of them.  Actually hit Best card Ever with this once, it was a great end of turn.

Bonus:  Since I mentioned Fixer, my favorite Guise+Fixer moment:  Fixer-Setback-Guise-Scraper is the order.

Fixer has Jackhandle, Crane, and Harmony in play and Grease Gun in hand.  Plays grease gun.  Guise plays Lemme see that with Tough Choices, borrows Grease Gun.  Sky-Scraper plays Compulsion Canister on Fixer for the awesomeness.

Next Turn Fixer takes his normal turn, then Setback plays Whoops, Sorry!, and destroys Lemme See that, sending Grease gun back to Fixer, for another round of no damage dealt by non-hero targets.  It was glorious.
